title: Research: delivery lower bounds for #968's frame-pair centers (no new κ)
head: ce9531beba1ce115fdcdc44925ded995a29b8bac
body:
**Research note: scoped negative result for one realization class, plus independent verification.** There is no κ claim and no supplier word. Main's selected κ (0.001661960547713947) is unchanged. Only `research/biframe-decoder-ladder/` is added.

#968 (themilkman216, merged) explains #717's cheap complex decoders (P111/63, P104/56) as frame-pair decoders and proves the exact 8-term floor. It prices P104's favorable budget at **+5.51% b** on T37, and says the PR589 bit cap leaves about 1.33% of b. It leaves building the asymmetric centers open. This package bounds that construction cost from below, for one explicit P104 decoder:

- **The cut is not common.** A P104 center gathers in u_b^⊥ while its readers span u_a^⊥. Theorem C's survivor is therefore ⟨u_a⟩: the cheapest copy tree drops u_b^⊥ → ⟨u_a⟩ at cost 7, and every reader must stand at a frame that contains u_a. Targets read 2–6 mixed centers (12/24/32/24/12 targets), and their cut frames have exactly that dimension. The coordinate decoder reads at frame 0.
- **Single barrier cut: ≥ 144 delivery copies.** A copy that is never dropped again can only climb, so it serves a chain of nested reader frames. Each center's 52 readers need 52 distinct frames (1059 incomparable pairs). Dilworth then gives ≥ 19 chains per center, so ≥ 144 copies beyond the 8 centers.
- **Staggered reads in one global order: ≥ 47 copies.** This is exhaustive over all 40,320 orders; the minimum is 55 chains.
- **Priced against #968's budget** at #717 P3's helper prices:

  | delivery | w8 | w9 | w9 merged | reaches the bit cap? |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | single cut (≥ 144 copies) | 7.3% b | 10.1% b | 20.2% b | never |
  | staggered (≥ 47 copies) | 2.4% b | 3.3% b | 6.6% b | only with width-4-priced copies |

  At shipped helper widths the single cut exceeds the 5.51% budget, so a barrier-cut realization cannot help. The staggered costs are inside the budget at no-merge prices, which leaves a window of at most about 3% b. Using that window needs a 104-port skeleton whose copies are exact, restored and frame-legal, at no more than ~79 copies at w9 or ~39 merged.
- **Independent re-derivation of #968's floor**, cst ≥ max(v − 48, 56) for v ≥ 96. The verifier was written independently of #968 and adds coverage:
  - all 11 #717 D3 hit files are shown to be exact bi-frames (#968 replays 3);
  - the label-span thresholds are enumerated over all 255 W(E8) support classes directly, with no flat-containment citation;
  - W(E8)-transitivity on the 2025 frames is checked;
  - new: the fully mixed frame pairs are exactly the unimodular root bases whose dual bases are roots (|det| = 1 on all 7168).

  #968 additionally proves the bound is attained at every p.

```sh
python3 -B research/biframe-decoder-ladder/verify.py            # ~35 s, standard library only
python3 -B research/biframe-decoder-ladder/verify.py --orders   # also re-runs the 40,320-order search (~6 min)
```

The expected last line is `PASS_BIFRAME_DECODER_LADDER: P104 centers need >= 144 delivery copies at a single cut, >= 47 staggered; #968 floor cst >= max(v - 48, 56) re-derived; 11 #717 decoders are exact bi-frames; 10 controls`.

**Validation**
- Fresh `git archive` replays of this head pass on Python 3.10.21 and 3.14.7, and the receipt is byte-identical on both.
- `--orders` passed on Python 3.12.14. That run was on the pre-reframe commit, whose order search is unchanged.
- `scripts/verify_selected_result.py` passes.
- Tampering is rejected: changing a vendored byte or the receipt makes the check fail.
- Controls:
  - negative: a corrupted coefficient, swapped columns, an un-punctured root, a flipped label, tampered bytes, and a frame of the wrong class;
  - sharpness: the 25- and 14-line thresholds are attained;
  - equality: the coordinate decoder costs 64 on P112 and 72 on P120.
- Not run: repository-wide `make verify` (no existing file changes), hosted CI, and Lean.

**Scope**
- The delivery bounds hold in the copy-chain model, for one explicit P104 decoder, under a single cut or staggered global phases.
- Not covered: the other mixed P104 decoders, per-target schedules, copies that are dropped again (which add copy rank), E-graph-only exactness, n ≥ 9 terms, |Π| ≥ 25, and the bit side.
- The helper prices are #717's measurements at #649, not re-derived on T37. The budget figures are #968's; its README is pinned by sha256.
- All inherited conditions remain. This is not a formal proof of the multiplication theorem.

**Pins and overlap**
- Developed on `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60` and rebased without conflicts onto main `2921874911956718fcaaaf9396fe8267b3cfa9f0`. The package shares no files with main.
- #717's 11 hit files are pinned at `67e9e846` (identical at `07f4671a`) by git blob id and sha256. Main's #595 `cert.py`/`skel.py` and #968's README are pinned by sha256.
- Assignment seed **47** (structural decoder research). There was no pinned coordination issue, so the claim is recorded locally in `CLAIM.md`.
- #968 drew the same seed and reached the same floor. It was opened at 11:17 EDT and merged at 11:57 EDT on 2026-10-13. This package's floor, census and delivery bounds were committed locally at 01:53 EDT, but submitted only now, so the floor's credit goes to #968.
- Overlap was checked through #1069. #998 (complex single lifts on P112) and #969 cite #968 for other objects, and #899 and #825 cite #717 for other objects. No PR prices the construction of #968's centers.

**Credit and disclosure.** The floor and the family are #968's. The decoders and the P104/56 observation are #717's (DreamingOfClouds), along with the B14 model, the S4 center semantics and the P3 prices. This package also builds on #595 (ceiling code), #446 (Theorem C), #620 (GamingPuzzled) and the E8 complex-unit lineage.
